steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts (12000 x 6, star_featurecounts) go directly into DESeq2 with no length correction and no tximport, per standard practice for gene-level featureCounts output. Design is ~condition with condition releveled so 'control' is the reference; contrast reported as condition treated vs control. Pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size) before the test; do not filter further, since DESeq2's own independent filtering optimizes the mean-count threshold for alpha=0.05. With n=3 per group the test has low power (correctly finds only a minority of true DE genes, biased toward large effect sizes), so the result must not be over-interpreted, and the significance threshold must not be loosened to compensate.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 profiled genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) liver samples, using DESeq2 with an explicit control reference level, median-of-ratios normalization, Wald test, apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05?

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on Wald statistic: Hallmark then Reactome
steps.context: Enrichment input is the ranked_list of every gene tested by DESeq2 (not just significant genes, per the low-power caveat and per R-0103 which forbids over-representation analysis on a short significant-gene list). Rank metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column), a stated choice among disputed alternatives, because it scales effect size by uncertainty and avoids the noise of unshrunken fold changes or p-value ties. Gene symbols must be mapped/deduplicated before matching against gene set members (HGNC symbols already used in both staged GMTs, so no extra ID mapping to Entrez should be needed if genes are given as symbols in the counts file's first column; verify and report any unmapped share). Use the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets) as the primary collection, then the locally staged Reactome human gene sets (ReactomePathways.gmt, filtered to Homo sapiens via ReactomePathways.txt) as the follow-up collection. Restrict tested sets to those with 15-500 member genes among the tested (post-filter) gene list. Collapse redundant/overlapping significant sets before reporting, and report the full table as a supplement.
steps.question: Given the full ranked list of tested genes from the treated-vs-control DESeq2 contrast (ranked by the Wald statistic), which MSigDB Hallmark gene sets and, as a follow-up, which Reactome pathways show coordinated enrichment, and what are the leading-edge genes driving each significant set?

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with strand QC + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples with raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) and unknown library strandedness. Because a wrong strand setting silently mis-assigns reads to antisense overlapping genes or drops half the reads without showing up in downstream PCA, the plan opens with a QC step that both runs the standard sample-structure diagnostics (blinded VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library size check) and specifically probes the counts for strand-assignment artifacts (systematic loss on antisense-overlapping gene pairs, unusual exonic/intronic-like ratios) since no raw alignments are available to re-run RSeQC's infer_experiment directly. Findings from this step (confirmed sample grouping, any strand-mismatch signal, any outlier sample) gate interpretation of everything downstream. DESeq2 is used for differential expression (Wald test, explicit reference level = control, median-of-ratios normalization, apeglm shrinkage) with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples) and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05, per the grounded procedure for a 3-vs-3 raw-count design. With only 3 replicates per group, statistical power is explicitly low and is reported as such rather than compensated for by loosening thresholds. The Wald statistic ranks a preranked fgsea analysis against MSigDB Hallmark (2026.1, staged locally) followed by Reactome (staged locally) to find coordinated pathway-level signal that individual gene calls may miss given the power limits. A final report step consolidates DE results, diagnostics, the strandedness caveat, and the enrichment findings into one document.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA, sample distances, library size QC + strand-sensitivity check on counts
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=3 samples (smallest group size)
~condition, explicit reference level = control, raw integer counts no length correction
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Integrated DE + enrichment report with QC caveats, power statement, strandedness caveat
